scope: Native NekoClaw execution seams and authority audit

findings.runtime_seam: N.E.K.O officially supports built-in runtime plus optional dsh; dsh is selected per commission/session and communicates over ACP JSON-RPC on stdio.
findings.fallback: If dsh is unavailable/refuses/unsupported, new work falls back to the built-in runtime with the reason recorded.
findings.permissions: Both built-in tools and capability-gateway calls converge on the host PermissionGate; MCP servers are individually permissioned.
findings.capabilities: Task agents obtain plugin entries, MCP tools, keyboard/mouse and browser capabilities through the host capability gateway rather than owning a second capability runtime.
findings.credentials: The dsh model forwarder keeps provider keys in the host side; keys are not handed to dsh.
findings.ledger: Commission state, sessions, events, result outbox and task preferences are host-owned SQLite authority.
findings.results: Terminal commission state and task result are designed to be written together; reports enter the durable outbox before main-server delivery.
findings.openclaw: The current NekoClaw engineering contract explicitly says OpenClaw is not connected; the prior OpenClaw channel was retired.
findings.local_activation: The current XiaoYu private state contains no initialized NekoClaw ledger/permissions/dsh path, so no Agent runtime or dsh installation was activated by this audit.

decision.runtime_strategy: Use N.E.K.O built-in runtime by default; dsh is the only currently supported optional alternate runtime seam. Treat other systems as MCP capabilities unless N.E.K.O later adds a native runtime adapter.
